reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes the BitClub Network opportunity through online registration and an entry payment. It presents passive-income and earnings claims tied to business sign-ups, downstream recruitment, and transactions, using specific examples and a possible large payday to support participation. the available video evidence notes that the acquisition is conditional and does not establish that the cited earnings or outcomes occurred.

citations.quote: if you build a downline you will get paid
going to get paid when you sign them up
In my team I have a few coworkers around that made $1000-1500 in the first 20 days of the startup.
Second step is to register online and get the passive income.
And the third step is to send your application for verification.

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly uses conditional, non-guaranteed language rather than promising a fixed return. The possible $5 billion outcome is explicitly described as dependent on many things going perfectly, and the discussion acknowledges uncertainty in mining results, including that the company could hit zero blocks in a day. It also directly tells people who remain negative not to join. Those qualifications are inconsistent with presenting participation as a certain or risk-free gain. The audience is being given a discussion of contingencies, operational difficulties, and personal judgment, not an unconditional promise.

citations.quote: a lot of things have to go perfect
my advice to those people that that are negative, is to not join
It's possible. We can hit
It's possible. We could it 14 in the day

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats conditional language as if it were absent, but the cited statements do not establish a guaranteed return. “Will get paid” is presented in the context of a business referral arrangement, while the earnings example is expressly described as belonging to particular coworkers. The cited registration language also does not establish that money must be deposited or that anyone is promised a result. The presentation's warnings about uncertainty and its advice not to join if unconvinced are omitted.

citations.quote: a lot of things have to go perfect
my advice to those people that that are negative, is to not join

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not undo the central solicitation. A speaker can mention uncertainty while still directing viewers to register for passive income and describing payment for sign-ups and downline activity. The caution to negative viewers is not a substantive disclosure of financial risk; it simply filters out skeptics. Likewise, saying outcomes require things to go perfectly does not explain what happens to participants if they do not. The quoted uncertainty therefore does not change the income-linked recruitment mechanism.

going to get paid when you sign them up

opening.argument: The material is structured as an instructional company webinar answering questions about Bitcoin mining, Coinpay, security, equipment, and how the platform operates. It explains how businesses could accept Bitcoin and Clubcoin, how cryptocurrency could be converted, how mining capacity is expanded, and how the training system works. The speakers are responding to audience questions and demonstrating a registration workflow, rather than merely making a bare solicitation. The operational and educational content is substantial: it discusses platform use, mining infrastructure, security incidents, and planned cryptocurrency expansion.

citations.quote: What is related to Bitcoin
we can show them how to change it into whatever currency they want immediately
we're still planning for that
You've got the 3 key areas and the three keys

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the webinar instructional does not prove its primary purpose is neutral education. The platform explanation is repeatedly connected to compensation, recruitment, and entry into the program. The described workflow culminates in registration and passive income, while the training is framed as a way to develop a business and earn. Operational details can make a solicitation more persuasive; they do not by themselves convert it into a neutral tutorial.

citations.quote: Second step is to register online and get the passive income.
You need only two things to develop your business

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The supposed demonstration is not merely technical. The workflow is expressly tied to registration, verification, passive income, and business development. Explanations of mining and platform features supply credibility, but they do not remove the commercial call to participate. The presence of audience questions also does not change the stated purpose: viewers are told how to enter the system and pursue earnings.

citations.quote: The first step is just to close the profile on the system.
Second step is to register online and get the passive income.
And the third step is to send your application for verification.

opening.argument: The compensation described can be read as ordinary referral and transaction-based business promotion. A participant is said to be paid when a business is signed up and when that business processes a transaction, which resembles a commission for introducing customers to a payment platform. The discussion does not supply a concrete deposit amount, a guaranteed rate of return, or proof that viewers must recruit people to recover a payment. It instead describes businesses accepting cryptocurrency, conversion services, and a platform intended to facilitate payments. The available material therefore does not establish the defining mechanics of a guaranteed-return scheme.

citations.quote: every time they accepted one or club coin you're going to get paid
if you build a downline you will get paid
offer to register with this platform to receive the payment in Bitcoin and Clubcoin
a lot of things have to go perfect

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's own quotes describe compensation tied to sign-ups, downstream recruitment, and transactions, but they do not establish that the video is a fraudulent scheme rather than a referral program. No cited passage gives a deposit amount, guaranteed return, or instruction to pay money in order to unlock commissions. The possible buyout is expressly conditional. Without those missing mechanics, the evidence supports a commercial referral interpretation at least as well as the accusation.

citations.quote: every time they accepted one or club coin you're going to get paid
a lot of things have to go perfect

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing deposit amount is not decisive. The evidence still describes payment for signing up businesses, payment from a downline, and passive income after registration. Those are precisely the recruitment-linked features that matter; a scheme need not state a guaranteed percentage in the quoted portion to be promotional scam content. Calling the arrangement a referral program does not explain why personal recruitment and downstream activity are central to participant compensation.
